text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- According to the public service law, one third of police officers in the eastern Viru region will have to be dismissed in February because they do not have Estonian citizenship.
- 14 people have died of hypothermia this winter.
- The Defence Forces need better training, accommodation for officers and women recruits, commander-in-chief Johannes Kert said.
- The 150 million kroon loan loss of the North-Estonian Bank will be covered by the state at the bank's merger with Union Bank.
- Ardo Hansson, the new economy adviser to the prime minister, warns in an interview that too much confidence in economy matters could be dangerous.
- The transport ministry has decided to privatise a 30 km railroad track between Haapsalu and Riisipere.
- Union Bank shares rose to 57 kroons at the Tallinn stock exchange after news of a merger with the North Estonian Bank.
